label: fact
method: a walk of the folder: each tracked file's sha256, and the map files made from them
map_files_note: snapshots[].file, tracks[].file, wind_hours[].file, runways.json and movements.json are written by the build from the tracked files listed in files[] (tools/flights-map.mjs), so they are served beside this index but are not in git and not in api/v1.
about: Every flights file: what it covers, its size and sha256. Replay: crosswind.json (the airports' wind on each runway, hour by hour, with departures), wind/<area>-<date>.json (the wind field), snapshots/<date>/<HH>.json (airline aircraft every 10 minutes within 40 nm of Lisbon and 30 nm of Madeira, from adsb.lol (ODbL), from 11 November 22:23 UTC), frames/<area>/<date>/<HH>.json (from 11 November about 23:45 UTC: Lisbon 250 nm every 5 minutes, Madeira 150 nm every 20, airline flights plus every other aircraft as an anonymous position; compact rows under a header of fields). Built beside it: map/snapshots/ (one per snapshot or frame) and tracks/<area>/<date>/<HH>.json (each airline flight's measured points in the hour, with first and last seen, altitude, speed, heading and phase now). Read README.md beside it for the shapes.
not_a_warning_service: Not a warning service. No forecast or advice of ours. Your airline decides whether your flight runs: its site or app has the latest. For warnings follow IPMA and ANEPC.
attribution: Aircraft positions: adsb.lol (https://adsb.lol), community ADS-B data, licensed under the Open Database License (ODbL) v1.0 (https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/1-0/). Our snapshots are a derived database offered under the same licence.

The OpenSky Network, https://opensky-network.org (M. Schäfer, M. Strohmeier, V. Lenders, I. Martinovic, M. Wilhelm, "Bringing Up OpenSky: A Large-scale ADS-B Sensor Network for Research", IPSN 2014). Used for research and non-commercial purposes, as its API documentation asks; its full terms page is still for a person to read (transport/sources.md).

Weather data by Open-Meteo.com, https://open-meteo.com, licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Its forecast API with past_days: the model's hourly analysis and short-range forecast, not observations.
